description: 360-degree orbit of the lunar south polar region (80-90 S, LOLA LDEM_80S_80M at 640 m) lit by the real Sun at 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z, with the preset landing sites pinned.
cameraAzimuthConvention: map bearing the camera looks toward, clockwise from 0E toward 90E; 0 = map orientation (0E up, 90E right)
honestyNotes: Heights are exaggerated 3x, so relief and shadow lengths are 3x the real ones; the Moon's curvature is true (sphere R = 1737.4 km).
Terrain is LOLA 80 m elevation block-averaged to 640 m; small craters and boulders are not resolved.
Lit by one Sun lamp from SPICE (DE440, apparent LT+S) with its real 0.53-degree disk and irradiance; grey Lambertian surface (albedo 0.12), no earthshine, no stars, no textures.
The Sun is fixed for the whole orbit; across 80-90 S it sets, so the side away from the Sun is in real night.
Pins are display markers, not to scale (about 14 km tall). Artemis III pins are approximate region centres.
